before.title: NCC 1982 — Pointy ideas with a solid point.
before.description: Introduce Color Pro 14 based on the February 1982 NEC PC-8853/JC-1410P2-class assembly, with AION digital-index/palette-to-RGB electronics and qualified 640x400 progressive Logix timing. New 64 KiB card retains previous features and adds 640x400x2 and 640x200x4; the remaining 1536 bytes hold up to 512 three-byte scanline palette entries. Horizontal and vertical retrace palette writes require explicit monitor capability and bounded timing. Launch the FlexiBUS two-button mouse with middle-finger vertical roller and thumb-side horizontal roller. Update AIONix and CP/M Platform Extensions/TUI to support pointing and standard-control activation without application source edits; statically linked libraries require relinking, and custom interfaces require adaptation. Release AION Entertainment Suite: Sudoku, Klondike Solitaire, Spider and FreeCell, with mouse-learning tutorials, keyboard alternatives and monochrome-compatible presentation. These titles and the dual-roller mouse are deliberate alternate-history offerings. June 7-10 Houston campaign: Pointy ideas with a solid point. Introducing the Logix Mouse. Point, select, and get to work. Colour business reports, hands-on mouse learning, partner compatibility demonstrations and professional graphics; AutoCAD remains a November target. Campaign plan and staged budget: ncc_1982_campaign.json.

outcomes.description: Demonstrate raster palette effects, unchanged standard-TUI controls with mouse input, and learning games. Keep later COMDEX high-resolution second-card/monitor plans separate; no unmeasured speed, cost or sales claims.

CP/M and AIONix TUI integration adds pointing and standard-control activation; static libraries require relinking and custom interfaces require adaptation. This outcome concerns software integration, not creation of the operating systems.
Release the Entertainment Suite implementations with the recorded mouse-learning and keyboard/monochrome support.
